policy_name: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
issuing_authority: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Executive Office of the President
regulatory_regime: US federal agency AI governance (OMB memoranda; AI in Government Act of 2020, Advancing American AI Act, EO 14179)
geo_constraints: US federal executive agencies (CFO Act agencies and other covered agencies)

locale_context.regulation: Binding administrative directive · applies to federal agencies only
locale_context.culture: US federal approach: innovation- and competitiveness-first, market-led, sectoral; policy set largely by executive action and swings with administrations; national-security and AI-leadership framing. Government-as-user governance (Chief AI Officers, inventories).

key_dates.event: Issued by OMB, rescinding and replacing M-24-10 (issued alongside acquisition memo M-25-22)
Approx. deadline (60 days) for agencies to retain or designate a Chief AI Officer
Approx. deadline (180 days) for agency AI compliance plans and AI strategies (CFO Act agencies) — not verified
Approx. deadline (365 days) for implementing minimum risk-management practices for high-impact AI, or discontinuing non-compliant use

covered_entities: agency AI Governance Boards (CFO Act agencies)
covered_systems: new and existing AI developed, used, or acquired by or on behalf of covered agencies
exceptions: AI used as a component of a National Security System
intelligence community elements (per memo scope) — verify
regulatory actions by agencies concerning non-agency AI use are outside scope
conditions: minimum risk-management practices apply when an AI use is high-impact (output serves as principal basis for decisions/actions with legal, material, binding or significant effect on rights or safety)
CAIO may waive one or more minimum practices with a documented, system-specific risk assessment, reported to OMB
objective: Direct federal agencies to accelerate responsible adoption of AI by removing barriers to innovation, strengthening AI governance (Chief AI Officers, strategies, compliance plans) and protecting public trust through minimum risk-management practices for high-impact AI.

related_policies.policy: OMB Memorandum M-24-10 (Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of AI)
OMB Memorandum M-25-22 (Driving Efficient Acquisition of AI in Government)

conflict_rule: Applies to covered agencies; does not supersede applicable law; national security systems handled under separate national security guidance.

clauses.section: Sec. 4(b) — Minimum risk management practices for high-impact AI
clauses.original_text: Agencies must implement the minimum practices in this section for high-impact AI use cases within 365 days of the issuance of this memorandum … The minimum practices include: conducting pre-deployment testing; completing an AI impact assessment; conducting ongoing monitoring for performance and potential adverse impacts; ensuring adequate human training and assessment; providing additional human oversight, intervention, and accountability; offering consistent remedies or appeals; and consulting and incorporating feedback from end users and the public.
clauses.requirement: test, impact-assess, monitor, train operators, ensure human oversight, provide remedies and gather public feedback for high-impact AI
clauses.condition: AI use case determined to be high-impact; within 365 days
clauses.exception: waiver by the Chief AI Officer with documented risk assessment
clauses.purpose: protect rights and safety; foster public trust
clauses.affected_asset: rights, safety and access to services of the public
clauses.applicable_systems: high-impact AI used by federal agencies
clauses.interpretation_notes: Wording not verified against a fetched official text (official hosts unreachable); close paraphrase/reconstruction. Section numbering per search summaries (Sec. 3 governance; Sec. 4 high-impact AI risk management) — verify. List of practices reconstructed from multiple summaries.

clauses.original_text: If a high-impact AI use case is not compliant with the minimum practices, the agency must safely discontinue use of the AI functionality until compliance is achieved.
clauses.requirement: stop using high-impact AI that does not meet the minimum practices until compliant
clauses.condition: high-impact AI not compliant with minimum practices
clauses.affected_asset: rights and safety of the public
